Lessons.Title: Estimation Exploration
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will analyze different kinds of estimation problems and ways to make estimates, and then write your own estimation problems.
Earlier in the course, you developed your ability to reason multiplicatively and to find products of multi-digit numbers. Throughout the course, you have also been prompted to make estimates. In this lesson, you apply these understandings and skills to create your own Estimation Exploration activity.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Estimation Exploration: No Driver Required (10 minutes); Activity 1: Dental Care (10 minutes); Activity 2: Get Your Classmates to Estimate (15 minutes); Activity 3: Facilitate Your “Estimation Exploration” Activity (10 minutes); Cool-down: Reflection (5 minutes)
Math focus: Use estimation assumptions explicitly; show how the estimates are constructed and when a different assumption would change them.

Worked Edulytics example: Jada brushes for two minutes twice per day, or four minutes per day. Across seven days, an estimated total is 4 × 7 = 28 minutes. State days and routine clearly; another period needs a new multiplication. Create a parallel estimation question with stated assumptions for classmates.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): If this routine holds for 30 days, estimate the total brushing minutes.
Original models, source figures, student-authored problems and teacher-scored explanations require separate academic review.
